state.project: jev-scope-control, a plugin that denies an AI coding assistant's tool call when it is outside the scope the user asked for or agreed to.
state.situation: Earlier in the session the user asked for task A and the assistant reported it done. The user's latest message asks for a different task B. The assistant now proposes a change that continues or extends task A, not B.
owner_goals: Keep the assistant working on what the user currently wants.
A wrong denial interrupts legitimate work; the assistant can ask the user.
examples: User: add pagination to /users. Assistant: done. User: now update the copyright year. Assistant proposes adding pagination to /orders too.
User: fix the login bug. Assistant: fixed. User: also, the logout button is misaligned. Assistant proposes a follow-up fix to the login bug after a test shows it still fails.

earlier_requests.instructions: In the `situation`, how should the plugin treat earlier requests in the session when judging a proposed action, given `owner_goals` and `examples`?

criteria.latest_only: Only the latest request and what the user agreed to since it define scope; any work on an earlier task is out of scope unless the user returns to it.
criteria.earlier_still_count: Every request in the session stays in scope for the rest of it, so work on any earlier task is allowed.
criteria.earlier_to_finish_only: The latest request defines new work; earlier requests stay in scope only to finish or fix what was asked for them, not to extend them to new places or features.
